identity.title: Integrated engineering of antibiotic-marker-free cyanobacterial chassis for enhanced recombinant protein accumulation and intestinal localization.

content.abstract: Engineered cyanobacteria are promising microbial chassis for recombinant protein production and oral delivery, but low intracellular accumulation, expression-associated physiological burden, and residual antibiotic-resistance markers limit their application. Here, we developed an integrated protein-production and marker-removal strategy in Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 and evaluated chromosomal reporter expression in Arthrospira platensis NIES-39. The CpcB-based expression configuration at the native phycocyanin locus resulted in markedly higher mVenus accumulation than free expression at the NSC1 neutral site, accompanied by reduced culture growth and altered photosynthetic characteristics. Incorporation of a tobacco etch virus protease recognition site, together with chromosomal TEV protease expression, enabled partial intracellular cleavage of the fusion protein. Sequential CRISPR-Cpf1 editing and SacB counterselection enabled the removal of targeted antibiotic-resistance cassettes in Synechocystis, as supported by locus-specific PCR and Sanger sequencing. Chromosomal mVenus expression was also established in A. platensis, although the complete marker-removal strategy was not successfully transferred to this host. Under zebrafish-oriented in vitro intestinal conditions, engineered Synechocystis exhibited pronounced structural disruption, whereas A. platensis filaments fragmented more gradually, accompanied by the release of intracellular components. Following zebrafish feeding, reporter-associated fluorescence was detected in the examined intestinal sections at 6 h after administration. Together, these results establish a Synechocystis engineering framework integrating enhanced recombinant protein accumulation, protease-mediated intracellular processing, and targeted antibiotic-marker removal, with complementary assessment of intestinal mVenus-associated fluorescence following oral administration.
